1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons, __the weapons stores processor panel further including a control panel with a master arm switch having master arm, safe, and off positions that control power delivery and fire signal generation to the weapons interface__.

2. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons interface includes a first weapons interface to a first weapon and a second weapons interface to a second weapon, the first weapon and the second weapon being of different types, __and wherein the weapons stores processor panel selectively enables or disables fire signals to each of the first and second weapons independent of one another__.

3. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 2 wherein: the weapons interface includes a third weapons interface to a third weapon and a fourth weapons interface to a fourth weapon, the third weapon and the fourth weapon being of different types, __and wherein the weapons stores processor panel selectively enables or disables fire signals to each of the third and fourth weapons independent of one another__.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a __MIL-STD-1760 standard, and wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements interlock logic that prevents fire signal generation when predetermined safety conditions are not satisfied__.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel, __wherein the laser pointer is powered through a laser arm switch on the control panel of the weapons stores processor panel__.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display, __wherein the data concentrator unit receives weapons status information from the weapons stores processor panel and integrates such information with flight management system data__.

7. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position, __wherein the master arm switch is mechanically or electronically isolated from the weapons interface such that the master arm switch directly controls power and signal generation within the weapons stores processor panel__.

8. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

9. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

10. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

11. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel, __wherein the laser arm switch is independent of the master arm switch and controls laser pointer power delivery__.

12. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including an override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position, __wherein the override switch selectively bypasses flight management system control signals to the weapons interface__.

13. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 12 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

14. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface, __wherein the weapons select switch operates in conjunction with the master arm switch to control which weapons are enabled for firing__.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction display, __wherein the display information includes real-time weapons status, interlock status, and master arm switch position__.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons, __wherein the weapons stores processor panel conditions and formats weapons firing commands in accordance with MIL-STD-1760 protocol before transmission to the weapons bus controller__.

17. (Currently amended) A vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) rotary-wing aircraft comprising: an aircraft mounted weapon; and an aircraft weapons control system, the aircraft weapons control system including: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of the aircraft weapon; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapon, __the weapons stores processor panel further including a control panel with a master arm switch having master arm, safe, and off positions that control power delivery and fire signal generation to the weapons interface__.

18. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel, __wherein the laser pointer is powered through a laser arm switch on the control panel of the weapons stores processor panel__.

19. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position, __wherein the master arm switch is mechanically or electronically isolated from the weapons interface such that the master arm switch directly controls power and signal generation within the weapons stores processor panel__.

20. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

21. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

22. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

23. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel, __wherein the laser arm switch is independent of the master arm switch and controls laser pointer power delivery__.

24. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including an override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position, __wherein the override switch selectively bypasses flight management system control signals to the weapons interface__.

25. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 24 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

26. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire in a manual over-ride mode, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface, __wherein the weapons select switch operates in conjunction with the master arm switch to control which weapons are enabled for firing__.
